chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Homayry quoted Al-Fazl ibn Amer on the authority of Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajaly, on the authority of Zarih al-Maharebi, on the authority of Aba Abdullah, on the authority of his forefathers (peace be upon them).
He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Three [people] if you do not wrong them, they will wrong you: the ignorant/common people, your wife, and your servant.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the three people that will wrong you if you do not express your discontent?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to illustrate the dynamics of power and expectation in daily interactions, emphasizing that neglecting to assert one's status or rights can lead to encroachment by those in subordinate or familiar roles. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on balanced authority (*sulṭān*) within the family and household, where kindness must be paired with firmness to maintain harmony and prevent exploitation by the 'common people' (*al-sufala*), wife, or servant.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-15 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted Al-Fazl ibn Amer onthe authority of Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajaly, on the authority of Zarih al-Maharebi, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB)
that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “There are three people who would wrong you if you do not express your discontent. They are the ignorant ones, your wife, and your servant.”
